public_rationale: Reporting published November 15, 2024 documents one executive's dissatisfaction with Copilot tools at an unnamed large Microsoft customer; it does not establish Fortune 500 membership [e1]. BCG's October 24, 2024 findings concern difficulty obtaining value from AI broadly, without identifying disappointment among Fortune 500 ChatGPT users [e2]. Computerworld's September 27, 2024 report on Gartner's June survey says most respondents considered Copilot somewhat valuable, but does not isolate Fortune 500 firms or rule out a substantial disappointed group [e3]. These items establish neither that a substantial group of Fortune 500 users was disappointed nor that such disappointment was rare through November 28, 2024 [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The unnamed customer account cannot establish how many Fortune 500 companies shared that experience [e1].
The broader AI survey does not identify the required company and product groups or directly measure disappointment [e2].
The Copilot survey covers companies of varied sizes, and its original Gartner report was inaccessible [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many Fortune 500 companies are somewhat underwhelmed by the real-world results they get from ChatGPT.

statement.excerpt: High school kids are still using ChatGPT to write term papers, but a lot of Fortune 500 companies are somewhat underwhelmed by the real world results they are getting.

from_speaker: the real world results they are getting
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that a substantial, non-isolated group of Fortune 500 companies found their actual experience somewhat below expectations. This does not require a majority, complete dissatisfaction, or an absence of useful results.
ChatGPT is the implied product. The accompanying discussion of GPT-powered Copilot makes that product relevant, but does not make all enterprise AI interchangeable with ChatGPT.

This is an ongoing observation as of November 28, 2024. The target is the most recent reportable experience through that date, including relevant earlier deployments. The source supplies no starting boundary, so none is imposed.
The assessment concerns the enterprise proposition supplied for grading, not the separate statement about schoolchildren.
criteria.support_condition: A credible survey identifying Fortune 500 users, or sufficiently broad documented company accounts, shows that a substantial group experienced results below expectations from ChatGPT or the GPT-powered workplace tools discussed in context.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence covering the relevant population and products shows that disappointment was rare or isolated. Successful deployments or a satisfied majority alone would not contradict a claim about a substantial disappointed group.

evidence.locator: Paragraph discussing customer reactions to Copilot's PowerPoint and Excel tools
evidence.explanation: This independently reported customer account documents dissatisfaction with Copilot. The customer is unnamed, so Fortune 500 membership and the prevalence of this experience cannot be established; no public primary account was identified.

evidence.excerpt: have yet to show tangible value
evidence.locator: Opening findings, paragraph defining AI leaders
evidence.explanation: BCG's survey provides evidence of widespread difficulty realizing AI value. It covers AI broadly across international companies, and failure to demonstrate value does not by itself establish disappointment among Fortune 500 ChatGPT users.

evidence.locator: Discussion of Gartner survey findings on Copilot value
evidence.explanation: This is material favorable evidence from a survey of 132 IT leaders at companies of varied sizes. It does not isolate Fortune 500 firms, and a favorable majority can coexist with a substantial disappointed group; the original Gartner report was inaccessible.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A credible survey or sufficiently broad documented company accounts identifying Fortune 500 users of ChatGPT or relevant GPT-powered workplace tools and comparing actual deployment results through November 28, 2024 with expectations. Evidence of a substantial disappointed group would support the claim; evidence that disappointment was rare or isolated would contradict it.
